candidates.exact_span:
The reasonable potential calculation was performed using test results for those parameters (tested
at MQL) that were greater than the MQL. Detection limit values were used for those parameters
reported as non-detect whose values are above the MQL. For RP calculation purpose, averaged
value of data set is utilized in the RP calculations. See the RP spreadsheet of the fact sheet
(attached).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Rules for substituting MQL, MDL/RDL non-detects, and using an averaged dataset in reasonable-potential analysis determine how reported measurements feed limit derivation; alternate interpretations of which values count or how they are aggregated could change the enforceable numeric limit selected for comparison.

candidates.exact_span:
However, effluent data for Total Recoverable Cyanide 6.28 ug/L (Estimated or J, 5/20/2020) and
(ND < MDL of 2.96 ug/L, which was below the MQL of 10 ug/L, 5/26/21), and (ND <RDL of
0.005 mg/L), with a geometric mean of 2.854 ug/L The limiting Wildlife Habitat and Chronic
Aquatic Criteria is 5.2 ug/L. As a result, the draft permit establishes monitoring requirements for
Total Recoverable Cyanide to obtain more data for later RP analysis.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage ties specific reported values (estimated/J, ND below MQL, mixed units), a geometric mean, a 5.2 ug/L criterion, and a monitoring-only outcome rather than a stated effluent limit; different readings of whether 5.2 ug/L is the operative enforceable limit, how non-detects and J-flagged results count, and whether compliance comparison applies would change limit applicability (A), whether monitoring is required versus limit-driven (B), and how missing/qualified results are classified (C).

candidates.exact_span:
The effluent data for delta-BHC were 0.00245 ug/L (5/20/2020), ND <0.002 ug/L (5/26/2021)
and ND <0.002 ug/L (6/2/2021) with a geometric mean of 0.0013481 ug/L. NMWQS does not
have numeric criteria for delta-BHC. EPA has not published recommended human health
criterion for delta-BHC.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Absence of state and federal numeric criteria for delta-BHC, together with qualified non-detect results and a geometric mean, affects whether any enforceable numeric limit exists for comparison (A) and how no-result or below-detection evidence should be categorized when no ordinary numeric compliance benchmark applies (C).

candidates.exact_span:
EPA proposes additional delta-BHC monitoring in the effluent to be used in the next permit
cycle should there be sufficient toxicological studies at that time to calculate limitations. As a
result, the permittee is required to submit a detailed plan to test for Delta-BHC at the source
water intake within six months after the effective date of the permit to both EPA and NMED for
approval. The plan must also include any use of delta-BHC at the facility, if any. Once approved,
the permittee must collect and analyze samples for delta-BHC at least once a quarter or more
frequent during the 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th year of the permit. The results of this study shall be
attached to the DMR reports to EPA.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Conditional and time-phased monitoring obligations (plan submission within six months, quarterly sampling in permit years 2–5, DMR attachment, source-water intake versus effluent) determine when monitoring was required; different readings of effective-date triggers, approval conditions, frequency, location, and reporting would change obligation applicability (B) and whether absent results reflect conditional non-requirement versus missing required evidence (C).
